Traditional Dmax (Cheng et al. 1992): finds the point on the lactate curve with the maximum perpendicular distance from a line connecting the first and last data points. Estimates LT2.
Modified Dmax (Dmod) (Bishop et al. 1998): same perpendicular-distance calculation, but the start of the reference line is the first measured point at least 0.4 mmol/L above resting/baseline lactate (or above the first measured point when no baseline is entered). The endpoint is the final measured point. Estimates LT2.

HAPLab Metabolic Analyzer · User Guide

Getting Started

HAPLab Metabolic Analyzer is a web-based data reduction and reporting tool designed for exercise physiologists and researchers. It integrates Parvo TrueOne 2400 metabolic cart data with lactate measurements, allowing users to manually identify ventilatory and lactate thresholds through interactive visualization. The tool automatically calculates and reports physiological parameters at user-defined thresholds, generates training zones, and provides longitudinal comparison of pre- and post-intervention testing, eliminating the need for manual calculations and separate spreadsheets.

Supported File Formats

  • Raw Parvo TrueOne 2400 CSV export
  • Cleaned/reformatted CSV files
  • Saved JSON session files (.json)

Quick Start

  1. Load a CSV file using the Load Session button
  2. Review metabolic charts and auto-detected VT1/VT2 thresholds
  3. Adjust thresholds by dragging the blue (VT1) and red (VT2) dashed lines on any chart
  4. Enter lactate data in the Lactate Analysis table if collected during the test
  5. Save your session as JSON for future use via Save Session

Loading Data

CSV Column Detection

The app uses flexible column detection and automatically identifies columns by pattern matching. Column names do not need to be exact. Columns are grouped into three tiers:

Data FieldDetected When Column Contains
● Tier 1 · Core (required for basic analysis)
Time (min)Column named "TIME" or containing "min"
Heart Rate (bpm)Contains "HR" as a standalone word (not "RR")
VO2/kg (mL/kg/min)Contains "VO2" and "kg"
RERColumn named "RER"
● Tier 2 · Recommended (enables additional charts and metrics)
Minute Ventilation VE (L/min)Contains "VE STPD" or "VE" + "L/min"
VE/VO2Contains "VE" and "VO2" (but not "kg")
VE/VCO2Contains "VE" and "VCO2"
CHO Oxidation (g/min)Contains "CHOmin" or "CHO" + "min"
FAT Oxidation (g/min)Contains "FATmin" or "FAT" + "min"
● Tier 3 · Optional (not currently used in calculations)
%CHO (%)Contains "CHO" and "%"
%FAT (%)Contains "FAT" and "%"
PetCO2 (mmHg)Contains "PetCO2"
PetO2 (mmHg)Contains "PetO2"
If a Tier 1 or Tier 2 column shows as Not Detected, the corresponding chart will be skipped. Tier 3 columns are recognized and parsed but not currently used in any charts or calculations, retained for future features. Ensure your column headers contain the key terms listed above.

CSV File Types

  • Raw Parvo export: app auto-detects header rows and column names, load directly without modification
  • Cleaned CSV: column names are matched by pattern, exact names are not required
  • Speed column: accepts MPH or km/h; a unit toggle is available in the Lactate Analysis section

JSON Session Files

  • Contains all metabolic data, lactate entries, threshold positions, and settings
  • Load via the Load Session button, restoring the session exactly as saved
  • Recommended workflow: save after each testing session and reload for report generation

Comparison Sessions

  • Load a second session via + Load Comparison
  • Both sessions should be from the same protocol type for meaningful comparison
  • Accepts both CSV and previously saved JSON session files

Metabolic Charts

Chart Descriptions

  • RER vs Time: Respiratory Exchange Ratio over test duration. RER crossing ~1.0 indicates maximal carbohydrate oxidation.
  • VE/VO2 and VE/VCO2 vs HR: Ventilatory equivalents used for VT1/VT2 detection. VT1 = nadir of VE/VO2 without rise in VE/VCO2. VT2 = simultaneous rise in both.
  • FAT & CHO Oxidation vs HR: Substrate utilization rates. The crossover point indicates a metabolic shift toward carbohydrate dominance.
  • Minute Ventilation vs HR: VE inflection points correspond to ventilatory thresholds.
  • VO2/kg vs Time: Oxygen uptake progression. A plateau may indicate VO2max attainment.
  • VO2/kg vs HR (Cardiac Efficiency): Rightward shift between tests indicates improved cardiac efficiency at the same oxygen demand.

Adjusting VT1 / VT2

  • Drag the blue dashed line to set VT1 (Aerobic / First Ventilatory Threshold)
  • Drag the red dashed line to set VT2 (Anaerobic / Second Ventilatory Threshold)
  • All charts, tables, and training zones update instantly when lines are dragged
  • Click the expand icon (↗) in the corner of any chart to enlarge it
  • Use arrow keys or scroll to navigate between charts in expanded view

Lactate Analysis

Entering Lactate Data

  • Enter one lactate value per stage in the Lactate (mmol/L) column
  • Resting lactate can be entered separately in the field above the table
  • Blank stages are excluded from curve fitting
  • Speed units toggle (km/h / mph) available above the lactate charts

Polynomial Regression

  • App fits 2nd or 3rd degree polynomial to lactate data (toggle available)
  • R² value shown on each chart, values >0.95 indicate excellent fit
  • Poor fit (R² <0.92) may indicate outliers or insufficient data points (<4 stages recommended)

Dmax Methods

  • Traditional Dmax (Cheng 1992): maximum perpendicular distance from a reference line connecting the first and last lactate data points
  • Modified Dmax (Bishop 1998): same method but the reference line starts at the first point where lactate rises ≥0.4 mmol/L above baseline, making it more robust for athletes with flat early lactate curves
  • Enable Show Dmax Construction to visualize the geometric construction on the chart

Threshold Lactate Values

  • Polynomial: interpolated value from the fitted curve at the exact threshold position
  • Nearest Measured: actual collected lactate value from the closest stage to the threshold

Threshold Summary & Training Zones

Threshold Summary Table

  • VT1/VT2 values are interpolated from metabolic cart data at the exact threshold HR positions
  • Lactate values are shown only if lactate data was entered
  • All values update live when thresholds are dragged on any chart
  • VT = Ventilatory Threshold (metabolic cart); LT = Lactate Threshold (lactate curve)

Training Zones

  • 5-zone model derived from VT1, VT2, and peak HR from the test
  • Zone HR boundaries update automatically when thresholds are moved
  • CHO/FAT oxidation values averaged from metabolic cart data within each zone's HR range
  • Lactate ranges derived from the personal polynomial curve at each zone's HR boundaries
Training zones are estimates based on the GXT data. Individual response may differ in field conditions.

Longitudinal Comparison

Loading a Comparison Session

  • Click + Load Comparison and select a second CSV or JSON session file
  • Primary session shown in red (right panels)
  • Comparison session shown in gray (left panels)
  • A modality mismatch warning appears if the two sessions used different protocols

Adjusting Thresholds Independently

  • Each session's VT1/VT2 lines can be dragged independently on their respective charts
  • The Reset button restores original auto-detected positions
  • The comparison column in the longitudinal table updates when comparison thresholds are dragged

Longitudinal Comparison Table

  • Shows side-by-side metrics for both sessions
  • Green = improvement, Red = decline relative to the comparison session
  • Reference Speed: enter a fixed speed to compare HR efficiency between sessions at the same absolute workload

View Modes

  • Side by Side: each session in its own panel for direct visual comparison
  • Overlay: both sessions plotted on the same chart axes

Saving & Exporting

Save Session (JSON)

  • Saves all data, lactate entries, threshold positions, modality, and app settings
  • Load later via Load Session to resume exactly where you left off
  • Recommended after every testing session before closing the browser

Suggested File Naming

SubjectID_Date_Protocol.json
e.g. JDoe_20240315_GXT.json

Data Privacy

  • All data stays local in your browser, nothing is uploaded to any server
  • JSON session files contain all entered data including patient information
  • Handle files according to your IRB / institutional data privacy requirements
There is no cloud backup. Keep copies of JSON session files in a secure, backed-up location.

Tips

  • Do not modify column headers in raw Parvo exports, the app locates data by matching the exact header pattern.
  • Blank lactate cells are treated as missing, not zero; only filled cells are included in curve fitting.
  • Speed can be in MPH or km/h, a unit toggle is available in the Lactate Analysis section above the charts.
  • Save your session as JSON after entering lactate data to avoid re-entry next time.

Methods & Calculations

Threshold Identification

VT1 and VT2 are positioned manually by the researcher by dragging the dashed threshold lines on any metabolic chart. The x-axis position is stored as a fraction of total test duration (0–1). Variable values at each threshold are determined by the Threshold Variable Method selected in Analysis Settings:

  • Linear interpolation (default): estimates the value between the two nearest bracketing data points. Formula: Value = V₁ + (V₂ − V₁) × (t − t₁) / (t₂ − t₁). Accuracy depends on data point density near the threshold.
  • Nearest measured value: reports the single closest actual data point to the threshold position with no estimation.

The threshold time is an exact direct calculation (t = position % × test duration) — no interpolation or nearest-value estimation is applied to it. Only the physiological variables (HR, VO₂, RER) at that time point are estimated using the selected method. Click any HR, VO₂/kg, RER, or Time cell in the Threshold Summary for a full calculation breakdown.

Peak Test Values vs. Known Maximum

By default, %VO₂Peak and %HRPeak in the Threshold Summary are calculated against the highest values reached during this test (the peak test values). For a true maximal test these approximate the athlete's physiological maximum, but for a submaximal test they can substantially underestimate true percentages.

If you enter a Known VO₂max or Known HRmax in the Patient / Subject Information panel (e.g. from a prior maximal test), all percentage calculations reference that known maximum instead, and the column headers change to %VO₂max / %HRmax. The Training Zones Zone 5 boundary and %HRmax ranges also use the known HRmax when provided. Marking a test as Submaximal adds a banner clarifying that reported peak values do not represent the true physiological maximum.

Distinction: a peak test value is the maximum observed in the current recording; a known/true maximum is the athlete's established physiological ceiling. Percentages are only physiologically meaningful relative to a true maximum, which a single submaximal test cannot establish.

Stage Averaging

Values reported for each stage in the Substrate Utilization table are calculated using the Stage Averaging Method selected above the table:

  • All breaths in stage (default): averages every data point within the stage time window.
  • Final 3 min / Final 2 min: averages only data points in the last 3 or 2 minutes of the stage window, capturing steady-state response by excluding the transient onset period.
  • Final 60 seconds / Final 30 seconds: same as above using shorter windows, consistent with many published protocols.
  • Nearest measured value: uses the single data point closest to the stage midpoint with no averaging.

If a stage is shorter than the selected window duration (e.g. a 90-second stage with "Final 2 min" selected), all available breaths within that stage are used automatically. This is noted in the table row.

Training Zones

Five zones are derived from VT1 HR and VT2 HR:

  • Zone 1 · Recovery: 0 to 90% of VT1 HR
  • Zone 2 · Aerobic Base: 90–100% of VT1 HR
  • Zone 3 · Tempo: VT1 HR to midpoint of VT1 and VT2 HR
  • Zone 4 · Threshold: midpoint to VT2 HR
  • Zone 5 · VO₂ Max: VT2 HR to peak HR

CHO and FAT oxidation within each zone are averaged from all breath-by-breath data points whose HR falls within the zone's HR range.

Substrate Oxidation — Direct Measurement

When RER, CHO (g/min), and FAT (g/min) columns are present in the CSV file, values are read directly from the metabolic cart output. No estimation is applied. The Substrate Utilization by Stage table reports values averaged from actual measured data points only — linear interpolation is never applied to stage table values. The averaging window is determined by the Stage Averaging Method selected by the user.

Substrate Oxidation — Frayn Estimation

When direct substrate measurements are absent but absolute VO₂ and VCO₂ (L/min) columns are present, values are estimated using Frayn (1983) equations:

  • RER = VCO₂ / VO₂
  • CHO (g/min) = 4.585 × VCO₂ − 3.226 × VO₂
  • FAT (g/min) = 1.695 × VO₂ − 1.701 × VCO₂

All gas exchange values must be in L/min. Alternatively, if only VO₂/kg is available and body mass is known from the file header, absolute VO₂ is derived as VO₂/kg × mass / 1000. Estimated values are flagged throughout the app with an amber notice.

%CHO and %FAT Calculation

Substrate utilization percentages are computed in this priority order:

  1. Direct CSV columns (%CHO, %FAT): used as-is when present.
  2. From CHO and FAT g/min: %CHO = CHO / (CHO + FAT) × 100; %FAT = 100 − %CHO.
  3. From RER (Frayn non-protein RQ equations): derived CHO = 4.585 × RER − 3.226; derived FAT = 1.695 − 1.701 × RER; then %CHO = CHO / (CHO + FAT) × 100. Values are clamped to 0–100%. Cells derived via this method are marked with a † superscript.

This ensures %CHO and %FAT are always reported when any substrate-related data is available, and the source of each value is clearly indicated.

Lactate Thresholds

LT1 and LT2 are identified from the lactate–workload curve using two Dmax methods:

  • Traditional Dmax (Cheng et al. 1992): maximum perpendicular distance from a straight line connecting the first and last measured lactate points.
  • Modified Dmax (Bishop et al. 1998): maximum distance from a line starting at the first measured point at or above baseline + 0.4 mmol/L and ending at the final measured point.

A polynomial regression of user-selected degree (2nd or 3rd order) is fitted to the measured lactate data and used for all threshold interpolations and curve display.
